main_text.p: tempora ita fruatur, ut fit per illa inter-valla mentis fuæ compos: juramenta ab illo tunc præstita non minus obligant ad fui impletionem, quandiu contigerit eum recto rationis usu frui, quam si ab ho-mine sanæ & sedatæ mentis præstita fu-issent.
main_text.head: SECT. IV.
main_text.p: Casus 20 & 21.Casus Quartus & Quintus fuit de obligatione Juramenti, quo quis aut ebrius pollicetur aut iratus minatur se aliquid facturum, quod sobrius & pacatus fieri nollet. Ratio dubitandi est quod cum ad hoc ut juramentum aliquod obliget, requiratur aliquod saltem animi deliberati judicium: ebrietas & iracundia, quarum utraque est amentia quædam brevis, sic judicium perturbant, & rationis usum tollunt pro tempore, ut quoad alter crapulam edormierit, alteri nonnihil deferbuerit æstuantis animi dolor, neuter sane a furioso multum distare videatur. Cæterum de istiusmodi Juramentis illud imprimis certum est, neutrum genus excusari posse a peccato: sed utrum ebrietas aut ira[?] impetus peccatum quod est in illo jurandi[?] actu aggravet an extenuet potius

page.notes: The right edge of the column is cut off by the scan, so the last letters of several lines are lost (e.g. "minatur se", "juramentum", "edormierit", "imprimis", "possé", "potius"); the visible letters were read, and cut-off words are marked where uncertain. "jurandi" is read as one word split at the line end, with no clear hyphen printed. The "ira" at the line end is only partly visible. The lines "e / brietas" and "æstu / antis" appear split without a printed hyphen and are written whole. The small marks at the bottom left (below the text) are not legible as printed text and are left out. The catchword "nor" appears at the bottom right.
